issue.title: Streamed kitty-animation video player for the tmux artifact viewer

task_type_fields.proposal:
Add a streamed kitty-animation motion backend for the inspect-first video view (src/sase/ace/tui/graphics/_viewer_loop_video.py). ffmpeg decodes frames, and the viewer sends them as compressed kitty graphics animation frames through tmux passthrough into the pane-local placement. That lets `space` play motion inside tmux, where mpv's kitty VO cannot render (unwrapped APCs become pane titles; uncompressed RGB is ~1,400x the H.264 bytes; window-coordinate placement lands on the wrong split).

Two gates must pass before implementation: (1) a real-kitty rendering spike proving correct pane placement and acceptable SSH+tmux bandwidth, and (2) demonstrated user demand once inspect-first has shipped. Follow the wire-format rules in the research report research:202611/fast_video_artifact_pane/fast_video_artifact_pane.md (Phase 3). Epic sase-1tb reserved the backend value `kitty` for this streamer; `ace.artifact_file_viewer.video.backend` accepts only `auto | poster | mpv` until it exists.

Proposed by phase bead sase-1tb.6 (motion-handoff) note #1 and routed here by the sase-1tb land agent.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Epic sase-1tb (fast inspect-first video artifacts) deferred this explicitly in its plan's "Deferred" list and its non-goals ("No streamed kitty animation in this epic"). The work also needs a spike and evidence of demand before anyone builds it.

issue.creation_reason: Epic sase-1tb deferred in-tmux motion playback to a future streamer; phase sase-1tb.6 proposed it as a follow-up and the epic lander is routing it to the backlog.
